This page sets the editing standards for everyone who writes on the SWCCG Wiki, human or AI. The same rules apply to all editors. The wiki is an encyclopedia: a compendium of existing knowledge that is honest about where the knowledge comes from. Editors do not invent knowledge.

== Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching) ==
'''Bill (2026-10-12; repeated many times):''' SWCCG is a small world. If a match is about '''99.8%''' likely to be the same person, treat them as one person and go with it. '''Never ask Bill to confirm near-certain matches.''' Skip only genuinely ambiguous cases.

'''State near-certain matches plainly (Bill, 2026-10-13):''' once a match passes this rule, write it as fact. Do not add "(inferred)", "matched by name" or conflict/hedging notes on pages, tables or Talk pages. Keep factual spelling-variant notes (e.g. listed as "Clint Hayes").

This covers '''all''' identity matching:
* '''Name variants:''' nickname or short form, middle initial, obvious typo, same events (Charlie/Charles, Matt/Matthew).
* '''Nicknames and handles:''' forum shorthand (for example "BFred" for [[Brian Fred]]), and GEMP, Holotable, DeckTech, or Slack handles when context makes the match near-certain.
* '''Photo identification:''' a tag or caption, the person's own comment, elimination within a tagged group, a nickname or handle plus thread or event context that makes the person near-certain, '''or''' a distinctive name plus a Decipher or SWCCG link (for example, a Decipher staffer of that name), with the reasoning in the shared photo-dest ledger (Bill, 2026-10-27; procedure updated 18 November 2026). A photo may come from any source. Uncertain faces stay unidentified.
* '''Exact name + Star Wars CCG Facebook group (Bill, 2026-10-30):''' an exact legal-name match already on the wiki who is a member of facebook.com/groups/starwarsccg is the same person; dest. Group membership is a Decipher/SWCCG link. Hometown match is extra color, not a gate. A public Intro with no SWCCG text does not block. Worked: [[John Petelle]]. Still skip locked identity traps and inexact names (Caputo ≠ Caputa).
* '''Decklist and results attribution:''' last-name-only sheets, first name plus initial, Username boxes, and published nicknames — merge onto the identified player page when context makes the match about 99.8%.

One canonical page per person; other names redirect. Link as <code><nowiki>[[Canonical|Name as in source]]</nowiki></code>. Add an "also known as" or handle note on the person page.

'''Conflicting spellings.''' When name variants conflict, compare the sources (results, forums, decklists, videos) and use the best-supported name for the page; the other spellings are redirects, with a "sometimes spelled" note on the page. Example: [[JW Millet]] (also published as J.W. Miller and JD Millet).

== Write for the reader ==
* '''Reader value decides what stays.''' Include a fact if it changes what a player understands or what a collector does. Cut it if it does not, even when it is true and sourced. Catalog bookkeeping, such as a rarity code or how an encyclopedia labels a pack slot, is not reader value.
* '''Be concise.''' Use short, neutral sentences. Cut repetition and unnecessary detail. Cut words before facts. When a source has a long list, put it in one sentence and move on. Clarity and full understanding come first: a sentence or quote may be as long as clarity needs (Bill, 2026-10-26).
* '''Describe the subject, not the sources.''' Write "X is Y", not "The Encyclopedia lists X as Y". Where the information came from belongs in the citation.
* '''Minor facts are welcome.''' Many readers collect and never played, so short, sourced collector and pack facts, such as the original price of a pack, add to the article.
* '''Give an example for an unusual rule.''' A concrete example makes a strange concept clear, for example "if both cards were in hand, they would be lost to [[Monnok]]". Not every rule needs one.
* '''Lead with the fact (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' The first sentence says what the subject is and the most important thing about it. Context and background come after the facts, never before.
* '''State facts plainly.''' When a reliable source, or Bill's own knowledge, supports a fact, state it directly ("Decipher showed Lucasfilm the card"). Do not soften it with "reportedly", "is said to", "appears to", or labels such as "soft" or "secondary". If a claim is genuinely disputed, name who says it ("According to Holland, ...") once, then move on.
* '''No research notes in articles.''' The article body never contains process or meta text: no "research note", "this pass", "this page does not invent", "not found", "no source says", "unverified", and no Gaps, Open questions, Research, or Sources-checked sections. Open questions and empty searches go on the Talk page under Missing data.
* '''Do not describe what an image shows.''' Captions identify the subject and credit the photographer ("Sealed first-series box. Photo: KaosBound."). Do not narrate visible content (art, colours, frames, which box is on the left). Quote printed text only when the text itself is the fact.
* '''Captions don't say where a picture came from (Bill, 2026-11-04).''' Don't write "from LinkedIn", "his Facebook photo", "Photo: Reddit" or "Fair-use screenshot" in a caption, and don't put the source ref there. Just post the picture with its caption. The source, the Preserved copy and any fair-use note go on the File page. A photographer credit stays ("Photo: Decipher.", "Photo: teabo.").
* '''Length discipline.''' Give readers enough sourced detail to understand the subject. Cover the people, chronology, relationships, features and concrete work that explain its significance. Add relevant detail when an article is too thin. Use prose for context and tables for catalogs or comparisons. Give each fact one clear home.
* '''End directly.''' The last section ends on a fact, usually the outcome or the current state. No summary paragraph, no caveats, no "more research is needed".
* '''One reference list.''' Use the References section only; do not add a separate Sources list that repeats it.
* '''Filler check before saving.''' Search the body for "note", "research", "pass", "not found", "no source", "unverified", "soft", "reportedly", "appears", "Gaps", "Inferred". Rewrite each match as a plain fact or move it to the Talk page. "Inferred" is still allowed as a Talk-page or reference note (likely facts may be published marked inferred there); just do not put an "Inferred:" label in body prose.
* '''Run the style lint (Bill, 2026-11-14).''' AI agents run <code>python3 authoring/style_lint.py draft.wiki --title "Page"</code> before saving and check the exact live revision afterward. Default lint remains strict. Fix every non-ARCHIVE finding. Pending ARCHIVE findings require the explicitly approved, hash-bound publication gate described in the [[#Publication and preservation gates (Bill, 14 November 2026)|Publication and preservation gates]] section; retain actual warnings and never call an eligible pending report zero lint. Human editors may run the tool too.

== Cite your sources ==
* Important facts deserve a citation: numbers, dates, rules, and anything a reader might doubt. Not every sentence needs one.
* When a fact is well established, add the reference and move on.
* When a claim is disputed, doubtful, or an opinion, name the source in the sentence itself ("According to ...").
* '''Citation layout (Bill, 2026-10-20).''' Sources go in the References section as <code>&lt;ref&gt;</code> citations, each with its Wayback Machine Preserved copy inside the same ref: <code><nowiki><ref>[https://example.com/page Title], site (date). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020000000/https://example.com/page Internet Archive]</ref></nowiki></code>. An External links section is only for further reading, and its links are archived too. Only deck and event pages (decklists, tournaments, championships, Retro League events) keep a Sources section; every other page cites in References.
* '''Every cited URL requires a checked preserved copy.''' This includes lists, tables, body text and External links. Cite a timestamped Wayback or Internet Archive copy only after checking its actual content or exact file bytes. Source pages, File descriptions and thumbnails do not establish preservation of a public image original. Publication during an external outage follows the [[#Publication and preservation gates (Bill, 14 November 2026)|Publication and preservation gates]] section; it does not make pending captures verified.
* '''Private source documents (Bill, 2026-10-12).''' When Bill provides private source documents (for example, an organizer's email), host them under swccg.com/snapshots/ (for example, snapshots/email/) and archive them like any other source, with a Preserved copy.
* '''No personal email addresses on wiki pages (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Do not publish personal email addresses (player contacts, mailto strategy credits that only carry a private address, or emails embedded in Service rows). Keep callsigns, hometowns, dates, and citations. Drop an emptied email column. Exception: a clearly defunct, historically significant, non-personal address may stay (for example a Decipher corporate strategy credit such as joea@decipher.com).
* '''Don't narrate source disagreements (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' When sources differ, state the best-supported fact and cite all the relevant sources on it. Explain the discrepancy on the Talk page, not in the article. Avoid sentences such as "Decipher announced 11 July; the Players Committee gives only Summer 2001."
* '''Do not add inferences.''' If no source states it, it does not go in the article. Put the idea on the article's Talk page, labeled as an inference.
* '''Every image original needs its own verified archive (Bill, 2026-11-13).''' Preserve the exact full-resolution original of every public uploaded image on the Wayback Machine. This includes photographs, scans, card faces, recreations, logos, diagrams, animated and vector images, unused files and retained public file-history versions. An archived article, File description page, source webpage or thumbnail does not establish preservation of the original. Internal image links are included.
* '''Check the original bytes.''' Download the raw archived payload and compare its SHA-256 with the original for that upload version. A successful save request, an HTTP 200 response or an unchecked capture is not verification. Keep the exact original URL, version identity, byte count, hashes, verification date and timestamped replay URL in the preservation record. Reject HTML errors, login/challenge pages, thumbnails, stale versions and mismatches.
* '''Link the checked image copy.''' Each File page has a Preservation section linking the verified full-resolution capture, separate from source credits and source-page archives. Preserve accessible source originals too. Public older versions need their own verified mappings; do not publish deleted, suppressed or private versions.
* '''Track unfinished preservation.''' Keep sourced images and articles available while capture work is outstanding. Queue blocked originals for retry, record the exact reason and report them as unfinished. Include image preservation in upload and article-completion checks. Retain independent, restorable database and original-upload backups alongside Wayback.

== Accuracy ==
* Link card titles and use the exact card title, including the printing's own title (for example, the Alternate Image of [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo]] is [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo (AI)]]).
* Give a price only where it shows something, such as an Alternate Image against the regular printing. A pack's original price is welcome.
* Proofread and read the changes before saving.
* '''Always give the deck's format (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Every decklist page and table row names a format. If the source does not state it, use the smallest format that fits the newest set in the list and the date, and mark it "(from the card pool)".
* '''Deck format comes from the tournament.''' A DeckTech post date does not determine a deck's format; use the tournament's format. For example, every FreedomCon 2001 deck is [[Premiere - Reflections III]].

== Tournament hub layout ==
* '''Calendar order of days (Bill, 20 November 2026).''' On a tournament article, sections follow the event calendar: Day 1 / Swiss before finals / Top 8 Results. Friday side events before Saturday before Sunday. Within a Results table, keep finish order (1st, 2nd, Top 8). Worked: [[2023 World Championship]] (Day 1, then Results, then side events Friday–Sunday).
* '''Infobox photograph (Bill, 20 November 2026).''' Do not put the champion's winning portrait in the event infobox; that spoils the article. Prefer a trophy, logo, or venue. Dest the winner's photograph in Photographs and on their person page. Worked: [[2023 World Championship]] infobox uses the event logo; [[Hayes Hunter]] remains in Photographs.

== Holder and tenure tables ==
* '''Earliest to latest (Bill, 20 November 2026).''' Office-history and tenure tables (who held a seat over time) run oldest date at the top. That is a history, not a person-page results list. Worked: [[Players Committee advocates]].

* '''No repeated person.''' Never repeat a person across rows when their tenure is continuous; show each name once on the row where they belong so one line shows their full tenure.
* '''Merge identical adjacent rows.''' Merge adjacent rows with identical holders into one row with the combined date range.
* '''Close gaps.''' Check for gaps between one holder's end and the next holder's start; research the true handoff date rather than leaving a gap.
* '''One range, not capture dates.''' When nothing changed between documented dates, show one range from the start date to present (or to the last documented date if no longer current), not a list of capture dates. Never split a continuous tenure at a year or archive-snapshot boundary unless the role, team or title actually changed per a source.
* '''Same role, one row.''' Abbreviations or wording variants of the same role (e.g. Dev = Developer) are one role: merge into one row with the full name.
* '''Position first.''' In organization and roster lists, write every entry position first, then person (for example "Design Advocate: [[Chris Kelly]]"), including advocates, in the same format as team entries. Service roles inside teams (for example lead GEMP slicer) are positions too: write "Lead GEMP slicer: [[Jeremy DiPaolo]]", one sub-bullet per role, not "[[Jeremy DiPaolo]] (lead GEMP slicer)".

== Photos of people ==
* '''Photo sources (Bill, 2026-10-27).''' A photograph of a person may come from any source. The only test is how certain it is that the photo shows the same person.
* '''Small World Rule for photos (Bill, 2026-10-27).''' A distinctive name plus a Decipher or SWCCG link (for example, a Decipher staffer of that name) means the photo is taken as the same person. Record photo-matching reasoning in the shared photo-dest ledger; keep that research off Wiki Talk pages. See [[#Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching)|Standing rule]].
* '''Facebook photographs (Bill, 2026-10-30; worked: [[Charles Lund]]).''' Dest the photograph as the wiki File (lead and Photographs; caption is the name, or the words printed in the frame). Preserve a screenshot of the Facebook surface as it appeared (photo viewer or group post) as the Route C snapshot: a short yellow banner with the date and live URL, then that screenshot. File page: who, Facebook, date, live URL, Preserved copy. Identification research belongs in the shared photo-dest ledger, off Wiki Talk pages. The Facebook-chrome screenshot stays off Photographs.
* '''Photo difficulty is not a skip (Bill, 2026-10-30).''' Dest the best available photograph of the person. Tiny circulars, AVIFs, and low-resolution faces dest as JPEG; the wiki scales them. Worked: [[Jindrich Nepevny|Jindřich Nepevný]] 88×88 circular. Do not HOLD for a failed circular click, AVIF, "need a larger JPEG", or a two-person frame when the subject is identifiable.
* '''Repeating face in a group.''' A confidently identified person may appear in several group photographs. Make a portrait crop only for a useful lead or another specific purpose; other photographs retain their full context.
* '''Memes and logos are not the lead.''' Skip a meme, logo, or product circular as the person lead; dest a real photograph of the person from the same profile. Worked: [[David Shettlesworth]] fish photograph instead of the meme circular.
* '''Identify from evidence under the small-world rule.''' Name a person from a tag or caption on the source (or the person's own comment), by elimination within a tagged group, '''or''' from a nickname or handle plus thread or event context that makes the match about 99.8% certain (see [[#Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching)|Standing rule]]). Mark anything truly uncertain as unidentified rather than guessing.
* '''No obscene gestures on person pages (Bill, 2026-10-12).''' Do not put a photo that shows an obscene gesture (for example a middle finger) on a person page. Such a photo may be used only as an identification reference; do not upload it to the person page or display it there.
* '''Cite the source and an archive copy.''' On the File page, link the source photo or post and add a preserved copy (<code>Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/... Internet Archive]</code>). Record unfinished preservation in the technical ledger under the publication and preservation gates below.
* '''Credit the photographer only when known (Bill, 19 November 2026).''' Omit the photographer field entirely when the source does not establish who took the photograph. Do not write a blank Photographer line, "unknown", or "uncredited". A still from a video is credited to the video's creator (the Players Committee YouTube channel is titled Star Wars CCG; credit those stills Players Committee).
* '''New file names only.''' Never overwrite an existing file; check for duplicates on the wiki first.
* '''Hunt a lead photograph (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' When creating or expanding a person page, hunt a sourced photograph and put it on the page. Video stills from SWCCG shows are allowed; crop StreamYard nameplates, host picture-in-picture, letterbox, and empty background out of stills so a single subject is centered. Do not leave a person page without a photograph when a sourced copy exists.
* '''One clear lead photograph (Bill, 18 November 2026; captions 20 November 2026).''' Choose the best available photograph for recognizing the person. Prefer a suitable individual photograph; crop a group photograph when needed to show the identified person clearly. Use one lead portrait at the top as <code>&#91;&#91;File:Name.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Caption.&#93;&#93;</code>. The lead caption is context, not a repeated name. Date it only when the event or title does not already carry the year. Worked: [[Charles Hickey]] "Retro and Open Communities panel, 4 April 2026."; [[Jonny Chu]] "At the [[2026 U.S. National Championship]].". If the source does not establish which person to crop, retain the full photograph and state only the supported identification.
* '''Centered images of single subjects (Bill, 2026-10-16; restated 2026-10-17; measured 2026-10-17).''' A lead photograph of one person is cropped so the subject's head sits in the center of the frame. Measure the head bounding box on the original. The crop-box center must match the head center within 5% of the crop width. Crop letterbox, black bars, StreamYard chrome, empty background, other players, bags, and table until head and shoulders fill the frame (Shannon tightness: worked 230×208). After the crop, open the crop file; if you can name empty table, a bag, or another player on one side, recrop that side off. Worked: [[Kevin Shannon]] 2011 Match Play Championship crop. Worked miss: first [[Ray Bordier]] SAT crop (<code>File:Ray Bordier DecipherCon 1999.jpg</code>; face on the right, bag and other players on the left). If a hall-shot crop is still off after that gate, use the full original as the lead and keep the crop File on wiki unused. Worked: [[Aldrin Long]], [[Piergiulio Nardulli]], [[John Arendt]], [[Jason Burrows]], [[Stuart Jones]] (Bill 17 Oct 2026).
* '''Additional photographs after the results (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Extra photographs go in <code>== Photographs ==</code> after Tournament Results, Retro League, Appearances, and In print when those sections exist, before Community card or See also. Use a <code>&lt;gallery&gt;</code> in that section. Do not put a gallery between the lead and the first heading.
* '''Photographs extras are gallery thumbs.''' In <code>== Photographs ==</code>, extras use a <code>&lt;gallery&gt;</code> so they render as thumbnails. Do not put <code>&#91;&#91;File:…|thumb|left|…&#93;&#93;</code> or a raw File in that section: that floats a full-size picture. Worked miss: first dests of [[Allen Varney]] and [[Lester Smith]]. Worked: [[Michael Mikaelian]].
* '''Add good extras to Photographs (Bill, 2026-10-17).''' When a sourced photograph of a person is found, dest it. One lead; extras go in Photographs even when the page already has a portrait. Do not skip a good extra because a lead exists. Excess can be trimmed later. Worked: [[Gary Carman]] keeps sat14 as lead and the events-page <code>sw99champ.jpg</code> highlight in Photographs.
* '''Contextual person galleries (Bill, 18 November 2026; captions 20 November 2026).''' Add appropriate distinct photographs in full context to <code>== Photographs ==</code>, newest event first. Caption wiki-links the event. Add a year or full date only when the event title does not already carry it; add a day only when the source supports it and it distinguishes pictures. Do not write "Still:" on person-page captions (source lives on the File page). Keep "Photo: Name" when the photographer is known. Do not cap how many Files a person may have from one event; trim only redundant largely similar frames. Do not create a portrait crop for every appearance. A sole uncropped lead photograph may also appear in the gallery as part of its chronological record. Worked: [[Jonny Chu]], [[Scott Lingrell]], [[Hayes Hunter]], [[Charles Hickey]].
* '''Keep the original with a crop (Bill, 18 November 2026).''' Put the full original of a lead crop in the person's Photographs gallery. Do not repeat the lead crop in that gallery merely because it is the lead. Reuse the same original File on relevant person and event pages.
* '''Event galleries.''' Normally show each full original once, with identified people linked. Omit redundant portrait-crop entries from that photograph; useful crops can still serve person-page leads.
* '''Group photographs (Bill, 19 November 2026).''' When a source names the people in a group photograph, wiki-link every identified name on the File page description and on the event gallery caption. Use the source's order. Unidentified faces stay unlabeled. The 12-word caption cap does not apply to that identification list. Worked: [[:File:2024 Eclipse Major Top 8.jpg]].
* '''Event relevance (Bill, 19 November 2026).''' Event photographs need a concrete, source-supported connection to the event or its participants. A channel name or posting date alone is insufficient. Exclude generic food, packaging, sightseeing and travel filler with no direct event connection. Retain documented event activity, participants, gatherings, venue and meaningful event context. Food, travel and gathering photographs can qualify when their event connection is clear. If relevance is uncertain, show Bill the photograph with its source context and ask before including or rejecting it.
* '''Keep useful old crops.''' Replacing a lead does not automatically delete its earlier crop. Keep crops with a useful historical or presentation role, and preserve their full originals. Check image usage before considering an unused redundant crop for separately authorized cleanup.
* '''Photograph context and provenance.''' Gallery captions and File pages link the event where known. File pages retain the supported date, source and photographer credit when known. A crop links to its full original and records the transformation. Do not substitute an upload date for the event date.
* '''Publish within preservation batches.''' Once a photograph's source, identity, independent backup and publication checks pass, dest it to the event and identified people's pages as the batch proceeds. Record source, File and article revision links together; Wiki publication and checked external preservation remain separate outcomes.
* '''Heading is Photographs.''' Use <code>== Photographs ==</code>, not Gallery or Photos.

=== Publication and preservation gates (Bill, 14 November 2026) ===
Source accuracy, independent backup and external preservation are separate checks.

* Verify every asserted fact against the actual source. Hold unread or unsupported claims; honestly incomplete articles may publish their supported known fields, including Japanese cards whose missing fields are clearly marked.
* Before publication, independently back up the exact prepared draft and checked source/original bytes, and verify restore/readback hashes and byte counts. Register each source and public original version with the existing central preservation service, retaining durable object/job identifiers, owner, reason and continuation. Local staging or a queued backup request is not a restorable backup.
* An external archive outage alone does not block publication when the explicitly approved, exact-hash publication manifest passes. All non-ARCHIVE findings remain blocking; raw ARCHIVE warnings stay visible. Registration is not submission, submission is not verification, and an eligible report is not zero lint or preservation completion.
* After saving, verify the actual public revision and independently back up that exact revision, including resolved signatures, before marking content delivery complete. A prepared-draft receipt does not cover a later revision.
* Keep pending preservation in maintenance records, signed Talk notes and the tracker, not article-body process disclaimers. Add a Preserved copy only after checking the actual capture. Preservation completion still requires checked replay/original-byte evidence and File-page links for each applicable version. Existing preservation-specific acceptance criteria remain strict unless explicitly changed.
* All clients register with the existing central server owner; only that owner submits saves. Do not create another saver or bypass provider cooldown/authentication stops from another host. The authoritative AI procedure is <code>shared/swccg-wiki/archiving.md</code> in <code>billbisco/ai-team-skills</code>; the reporting contract is <code>docs/publication-preservation.md</code> in <code>billbisco/swccg-wiki</code>.

<span id="Photograph_File_pages"></span>
== Image File pages ==

The standard image File page uses ordinary sections beneath the image, without a boxed information table or collapsed source panel. This applies to photographs, card images, scans, screenshots, logos, diagrams and other image types. See the [[:File:2023 World Championship Masago lunch 14 August.jpg|Masago lunch example]].

* '''Description.''' Briefly identify the subject, for example "Group lunch at Masago." Add supported names as wiki links when they are identified, plus positions, event, date or exact card printing when they help identify the image. Keep source-publication details in the source section.
* '''Source and credit.''' Name the actual source publication, community, collection or website and link its source page or post when available. Credit the photographer, artist, scanner or other creator when established; use "Shared by" for a poster whose authorship is not established. When the photographer is unknown, omit that field entirely rather than leaving it blank. Distinguish the date created or photographed from the date posted. Omit empty fields and speculative authorship.
* '''Original access.''' Clicking the image opens the uploaded original. Do not add another "View full-resolution image", "Original photograph" or "Native photograph" link to those same bytes. A link to a different source, such as the uncropped photograph or containing document, remains useful.
* '''File information.''' Image pages omit the generated preview-size/resolution line and the Original file/dimensions/file-size/MIME block beneath the image. Keep technical information in file history or the technical preservation record, together with backup hashes and repository locations. A GitHub backup is not the visible source credit when it is only the storage copy. Non-image downloads retain their appropriate download controls.
* '''Classification.''' Categorize images by their supported subject and type; photographs belong in [[:Category:Photographs]] or an appropriate descendant category. Image presentation follows the actual image media type, rather than its filename or membership in a photograph category.

=== Additional information when needed ===

* '''Crops, restorations and composites.''' Add a Changes section explaining material alterations and linking the full original or component sources. Label recreations and generated illustrations accurately; do not present them as native historical images.
* '''Card images and scans.''' Identify the exact card printing or physical item. Preserve publisher, edition, language and recreation information that establishes which image is presented. Do not relabel a recreation as an original scan.
* '''Documents and distribution packages.''' Identify the publication, package or physical source and its page, panel or member path. Link the containing document or package when available; an extracted image alone does not replace that source.
* '''Screenshots and video stills.''' Identify the source page or video and the frame timestamp or capture date when supported. Credit the source's creator accurately.
* '''Specific credit or licence terms.''' Retain the source's applicable credit, permission or licence wording in Source and credit or a separate Rights section when needed. Public availability alone does not establish a licence.
* '''Preservation.''' Retain checked archive links in the appropriate Preservation section. Record pending work and technical verification in the preservation ledger; do not add boilerplate claims that an image is untouched or preserved without evidence.

Use only the extra sections that have substantive, supported information. When a description or source is missing, retain supported information and record the precise gap in the repair inventory rather than inventing facts or filling an empty section with boilerplate. Existing identity, privacy and publication checks still apply.

== Pictures for articles ==
* '''Find pictures for every article (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Event, place, set, mechanic, and website articles should carry relevant pictures when a sourced copy exists. Hunt for venue photographs, contemporaneous magazine coverage, player portraits from that event, product shots, related card images, and archived website graphics.
* '''Historic venue photographs.''' Public-domain photographs of a venue used for an SWCCG event are allowed (worked: Cavalier Hotel for the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]] and [[1999 Decipher World Championship]]).
* '''Venue photograph in the lead (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' An event article puts a photograph of the site in the lead. Two right-hand thumbs are allowed: the venue, and an event graphic or a later photograph of the same building. Worked: Cavalier Hotel on 1998 and 1999 Worlds; Virginia Beach oceanfront on [[FreedomCon]] and [[2001 Decipher World Championship]]. Hunt a contemporaneous licensed photograph first.
* '''Website screenshots and original graphics (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' An article about a website carries archived screenshots or original site graphics of the home page and major section pages when those copies exist. Prefer the original GIF or JPEG from the archived site over a screenshot of Wayback chrome. Worked: [[Decipher.com]] lobby image-maps and section banners.
* '''Split oversized website articles (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' When a website article is too large for one lead-plus-gallery, split major sections into subpages so each page can carry its own pictures. The hub keeps a short summary and a history gallery; the subpages hold the detail and the section graphics. Worked: [[Decipher.com]] into [[Decipher.com Star Wars CCG]], [[Decipher.com Galleries]], [[Decipher.com contests]] and [[Decipher.com downloads]].
* '''Straighten and crop.''' Straighten skewed scans so the subject fills the frame. Edit out magazine margins, adjacent cards, and card chrome from a portrait crop.
* '''Two lead thumbs plus a gallery.''' Two lead thumbs plus a gallery is enough. Do not leave an event page or a website page text-only when sourced pictures exist.
* '''Facebook groups (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' An article about a Facebook group carries a screenshot of the group (cover, title, and membership line). Crop out Facebook chrome and personal posts. Worked: [[Star Wars CCG Graded]].
* '''Person pages.''' Person-page photographs follow '''Photos of people''' (one lead thumb; extras in Photographs after the results). This section is for event, place, set, mechanic, and website articles.
* '''Where to look first.''' For event, place, set, mechanic and website pictures, search SWCCG-associated sources first. A public-domain historic venue photo is allowed when that venue hosted an SWCCG event. Photos of people may come from any source (see '''Photos of people''').
* '''Convention and multi-game event pages (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' This is an SWCCG wiki. Convention pages stay SWCCG-first: other Decipher games get a brief mention and a hub link. Photographs on those pages show SWCCG play, SWCCG people, the venue, or SWCCG prizes. Other-game-only photographs stay on that game's hub or on the person's page. Worked: [[DecipherCon 2002]].

== Tournament and league pages ==
* '''All service goes in the Service table (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Whenever a person page or a source mentions any service by that person, it must be a cited row in the person's <code>== Service ==</code> table, not just prose. Service includes tournament director, judge, Squadron or other volunteer roles, Players Committee or Decipher roles, event host, and GEMP or development work. Each row gives the dates and the role in the source's own words, with a reference. If the page has no Service section, add one just above the first section.
* '''Hosting a show is Service (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Creating or hosting a published SWCCG show or channel is a Service row. Being a guest on someone else's show is Appearances.
* '''Formats are single GEMP format names''', e.g. "Premiere - Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck" or "Premiere - Cloud City (Modified)". Link the exact format page if it exists; otherwise write the exact name as plain text.
* '''Standings''': show the top 8, with the full list in a collapsed table (<code>class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"</code>).
* '''GEMP handles''' go in a standings column, filled where known from the player's page or the sources; leave the cell blank if unknown.
* '''No handles in prose.''' Link the person; their page gives the handle.
* '''Newest first (Bill, 2026-10-13; restated 20 November 2026).''' On player pages, every dated list runs newest first: Service, Appearances, In print, Interviews subsections, Tournament Results, Retro League, Photographs, and decklist sections. Latest year at the top; within a year the latest item first (season standings and ROCS playoffs above that year's events). Do not reverse finish-order event Results (1st, 2nd, Top 8). Do not reverse history and tenure tables (earliest date at the top; worked: [[Players Committee advocates]]).
* '''Lead with the best result (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' A player page's lead opens with the player's best or most notable sourced result (a win, a top finish, or a season or ROCS title), not a weaker or older placement. Mention other results after it, keep it to a sentence or two, and cite it, reusing the result row's reference.
* '''Every decklist page needs a checked source and preservation job.''' Cite the actual PC deck page, GEMP share, forum post or Bill-provided source under Sources. Use a checked existing preserved copy when available; otherwise follow the procedure in the [[#Publication and preservation gates (Bill, 14 November 2026)|Publication and preservation gates]] section, with independent source backup and durable pending ownership. Never invent a source or archive capture.
* '''Unmarked cards are the original (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' In a decklist, a card or objective not marked (V) is the regular Decipher card: link the original printing (for an objective, its two-sided page, e.g. [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi]]). Link the (V) card only when the list says (V). If an objective is on the wrong side for the deck, it is a transcription error: leave the link and note it on the Talk page.


== Tournament reports (Bill, 2026-10-24) ==
* '''One article per report.''' A player's own account of a tournament (from DeckTech, a fan site, the Players Committee forum, a video, …) gets its own article, titled ''<Author> <Report title> (tournament report)''. It gives the author, publication, event, date, finish, record and decks, a table of the games described, and the original report.
* '''The report text is reproduced verbatim and uncensored.''' Only a crude page title is replaced (by author and event); the original title stays in the article.
* '''Every tournament a report mentions gets a page''' with what is known (date, site, format, players, winner, results) and a row on [[List of SWCCG tournaments]]. A side event covered in a report (for example a sealed event at Worlds) gets its own page and is mentioned on the main event's page.
* '''Every named player gets an article''' about them and what they played, with a Tournament Results row citing the report. The small-world rule applies: a named person is the same person as the existing page of that name. A player named only by first name gets no page.
* '''Reports update existing event pages:''' new participants, finishes, records, player counts, dates and sites, each cited to the report.
* '''Discrepancies:''' Decipher's records, and an event page's existing sourced record, are trusted over a player's report until there is more evidence. The conflict is noted in a ''Discrepancies'' section on both the report article and the event page.
* Each source has a catalog page (e.g. [[DeckTech tournament reports]]) and a category under [[:Category:Tournament reports]]; the overview is [[Tournament reports]].

== Appearances and In print ==
* '''Guest spots and written features (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' A guest on a video or audio SWCCG show, or the subject of a written feature, gets a cited row on their person page the same turn. The table is the mention, as with Service.
* '''Appearances''' (video and audio guest spots): heading <code>== Appearances ==</code>, table columns Date / Outlet / Title / Role, newest-first. Role in the source's own words, otherwise guest, co-host, panelist, or interviewee. Place after Tournament Results and Retro League (after Tournament Results when there is no Retro League; after Service or the lead when there are no results sections).
* '''In print''' (written articles and features): heading <code>== In print ==</code>, columns Date / Publication / Title, newest-first. After Appearances when both exist.
* '''Cross-reference the host catalog.''' Filling a Guest(s) cell on a host page (for example [[BoardMatt]]) also adds the matching Appearances row on the guest's page that turn.
* '''Interviews stay Interviews.''' <code>== Interviews ==</code> with <code>=== Outlet, date ===</code> subsections remains the write-up of interviews OF the person when there are two or more. A video interview still gets an Appearances row.
* '''Not every mention.''' The person must be a guest, interviewee, panelist, or named co-host who is there to discuss. Personal opinion lists are not cross-referenced. A first name with no last name stays unlinked (do not invent a person page).

== Anagrams on person and card pages (Bill, 2026-10-15; restated 2026-10-17) ==
Sourced printed-title anagrams of a person, a close family member, or a named pet get their own section. Worked examples: [[Tom Braunlich]] / [[Nabrun Leids]]; family table: [[Chuck Kallenbach]].
* '''Person page.''' Heading is always <code>== Anagrams ==</code>. Place after the last career or results section, before See also. Use the same three-column table as [[Anagrams]] (Card / Unscrambled / Relation). The table is the mention; keep designer leads on the career. Stubs whose only sourced fact is the anagram keep one sentence in the lead and still use the table.
* '''Intro sentence.''' Write the fact ("[[Nabrun Leids]] is an anagram of Braunlich" / "Printed titles scramble Braunlich's surname."), then the table. Cite [[Anagramed Decipherians]] and Encyclopedia 3.2 p.200 on that sentence.
* '''Family and pets''' stay on the same table, with Relation filled in. Each related person still gets their own page and their own one-row table.
* '''Only sourced rows.''' Copy Card / Unscrambled / Relation from [[Anagrams]] or a named Decipher source. Uncertain hub rows stay on the hub until the match is solid. Do not invent new anagrams.
* '''Card page.''' Always Template:Card <code>|anagram=</code> ("The title is an anagram of <nowiki>[[Person]]</nowiki>."). That renders <code>== Anagram ==</code>. Not under Also known as.
* '''Printed title.''' The Card column and the card page use the printed title. A short-title redirect is allowed (<code>[[R'kik D'nec]]</code> → [[R'kik D'nec, Hero Of The Dune Sea]]).
* '''Hub.''' [[Anagrams]] is the full list. Person pages list only that person's rows. See also includes [[Anagrams]]. No card art on the person page.

== Easter eggs on card pages (Bill, 2026-10-17) ==
Hidden jokes, call-outs, and extra images on a printing get their own section. Hub: [[Easter eggs]].
* '''Card page.''' One <code>== Easter egg ==</code> via Template:Card <code>|easter_egg=</code>, immediately before See Also. Omit when none. Two eggs on one card stay one section.
* '''Cite the fact.''' Cite Decipher Art Show 1999 (the capture you opened) as primary for Premiere through Jabba's Palace. Later-set eggs cite Encyclopedia 3.2. Write the fact, not the source. Zoom crop on the card.
* '''Hub.''' [[Easter eggs]] is the full list. See also includes [[Easter eggs]].
* '''Packaging.''' The Hoth display-box egg goes on [[Hoth Limited]], same heading immediately before See also.

== Card page titles (Bill, 2026-11-04) ==
One page per printing. Its title is the printed card title (no uniqueness dots), plus qualifiers only when another page would otherwise have the same title. Add them in this order:
* '''(V)''' for every Players Committee virtual card, as printed.
* '''Virtual printings:''' the current printing (the newest Virtual Modern set, or the only virtual printing) is plain '''Title (V)'''. An older virtual printing of the same card takes its set:
** Virtual Legacy: '''Title (V) (Virtual Block N)''', for example [[Well Guarded (V) (Virtual Block 8)]] next to [[Well Guarded (V)]] (Virtual Set 21).
** Virtual Original: '''Title (V) (Virtual Set N: Name)''', for example [[Hyperwave Scan (V) (Virtual Set 3: Revolution)]].
* '''Side:''' '''(Light)''' or '''(Dark)''' only when two cards with the same title are on opposite sides (for example [[Weather Vane]] and [[Weather Vane (Dark)]]). It is never used to tell two printings of one card apart.
* '''Decipher set:''' '''(Set name)''' after the side when the side is still not enough (for example [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere)]] and [[Sense (Dark) (Coruscant)]]).
* '''Printing marks''' last, as printed: (AI), (ALT), (Holo AI), (Errata), (PC Errata).
Do not create numbered duplicates such as "(2)", and do not leave short-form alias redirects such as "Title (V) (Virtual Set 3)". Link the full title, piping the text if needed. Decklists link the printing that was legal on the event date (see [[#Tournament and league pages|Tournament and league pages]]).

== Card versions vs products (Bill, 2026-11-10) ==
A '''version''' is the printed object. Two copies are the same version when language, border, '''set icon''' (Premiere has none), foil, printed game text and stats, and copyright year all match. A '''product''' is the box or pack. Leftover or repacked copies of the same version (Enhanced Premiere Unlimited boosters, First Anthology starters, Reflections I–III bulk non-foils) are extra products on that article. They do not get a new article or another title parenthesis.

'''Named editions''' of one version that were independently sold as constructed sets share one article. The title stacks those edition names in chronological order, first product first. English white Premiere with no expansion icon and ©1995 that shipped in both Premiere Two-Player (February 1996) and Premiere Unlimited (April 1996): [[Imperial Barrier (Premiere Two-Player) (Unlimited)]]. Unlimited-only whites stay '''Title (Unlimited)'''. Two-Player exclusives and the Electrobinoculars / Lars' Moisture Farm misprints stay Two-Player-only titles. Premiere cards reprinted in the Empire Strikes Back Two-Player Game with ©1996: '''Title (ESB Two-Player)'''. Death Star II Starter reprints of earlier titles with ©2000 are their own version. The Players Committee lists revised wording on some of those reprints (Monnok, Grimtaash). They are not a third parenthesis on the 1995 white. Japanese black Premiere and Japanese white Two-Player are two versions because the border differs.

Set hubs list every card the set contains and pipe the display name: <code><nowiki>[[Imperial Barrier (Premiere Two-Player) (Unlimited)|Imperial Barrier]]</nowiki></code>. Redirect the short names to the stacked title except where the short name is a different version (the Two-Player misprints).

Infobox identity block, top to bottom: '''Set''' (primary product, first named edition). Then '''Set icon''' (printed expansion symbol, or none). Then '''Also in''' (other products of this version; omit when empty). Then Publisher, Era, and '''GEMP ID''' (first named edition first; two ids when two named editions). Gameplay '''Icons''' (Pilot, Warrior) stay with the face stats.

GEMP: one wiki article and one uniqueness for one version. Two GEMP ids when that version is a named edition of two constructed sets (Premiere Two-Player first, then Unlimited). Leftover SKUs do not mint extra ids. A format can legalize Premiere Two-Player without Unlimited, and the reverse.

swccg-guild/work#244.

== Foreign-language card articles (Bill, 2026-11-05) ==
On English-language articles for a printing in another language, put a visible '''Title''' section near the top of the article body, before Card Text, showing the exact printed title in its original script. An infobox row is not enough.

For Japanese printings, name the translation section '''Translation of Japanese Text'''. Place it below Lore and above Notes. Translate the title, lore and game text.

'''Comparison with the English printing''' (Bill, 2026-11-08) is a short paragraph of real wording differences: a different number, actor, trigger, named card, or restriction. State the difference and stop. Do not restate the Title, Card text or Lore translations. Do not restate the English title. Omit the paragraph when the translations already cover the Japanese and the English is a straight counterpart. Do not add disclaimers such as "this comparison describes printed wording, not an official ruling".

Worked: [[Han's Dice (Japanese)]] (ability 2 or more vs greater than 2; cancel and redraw vs draw another instead). [[Baniss Keeg (Japanese)]] (numbered options; 意識操作 for Alter). Worked miss: first [[Lateral Damage (Japanese)]] restamp restated both printings at length.

== Card infobox Versions (Bill, 2026-10-26) ==
Template:Card '''Versions''' is the family navigator. Full lineage both directions. Omit the row when this printing is the only one. Dest remaining families in waves. Worked family: [[Luke Skywalker]].
* '''Closed prefixes''', oldest first: Decipher · Decipher (AI) · Decipher Errata · PC Errata · Virtual Original · Virtual Legacy · Virtual Legacy (AI) · Virtual Modern · Virtual Modern (ALT).
* Unmarked '''Decipher''' is the printed face. Do not prefix Original. '''Title (Original)''' redirects to unmarked print.
* '''Revised, Errata and remasters (Bill, 18 November 2026).''' Revised names the actual Decipher white-border edition; it is not shorthand for a later virtual publication. Errata identifies a sourced change to text, statistics, uniqueness or official replacement wording. A same-word improved Players Committee face is PC Remastered, with <code>(Remastered)</code> in its article title. A newer image, different file size or an E/E1 margin mark alone does not establish another gameplay state.
* '''Article title and printed Title field.''' Canonical article titles and Versions labels may qualify an edition or gameplay state. The card infobox's <code>title=</code> records the title printed on the card or its official virtual release-sheet label, including an official <code>(V)</code>. Keep an unprinted set name, side, Errata number or Remastered qualifier in the article title and version metadata. Preserve actual parenthetical names and official AI/ALT labels.
* '''Titles and labels agree.''' Apply that classification to the canonical article title, Versions label, printing metadata and change explanation. Correct a false Errata title as part of an authorized family repair, preserving page history and redirects. Same-word slip/composite copies belong on one article, with the full face first and the source slips and citations retained there. Number Errata states only when distinct sourced states require it.
* '''Errata authority and printing scope.''' Attribute replacement wording from the applicable primary Glossary, Supplement or Appendix. A later Players Committee reproduction of Decipher replacement text remains Decipher Errata; credit the image separately. PC Errata requires a supported PC replacement beyond the applicable Decipher wording. A correction explicitly limited to a white-border reprint does not automatically create an Errata state for its Limited printing. Resolve source-authority warnings before approving affected titles and labels.
* '''Complete replacement-state coverage.''' Check applicable complete replacement wording in the primary Glossary, Supplement and Appendix independently of existing articles, images and the proposed navigator. Match each distinct supported state to an article or a documented gap, respecting language and printing scope. Explanatory rulings belong in Rulings; they are not extra game text. A documentary state without a verified matching face keeps its image blank; do not substitute another printing. Use a stable <code>publication_id</code> and leave <code>card_uid</code> and <code>gemp_id</code> blank when no mapping is verified.
* '''Errata metadata.''' After verifying authority, use <code>version_label=Decipher Errata</code> or <code>version_label=PC Errata</code>. Put the document name and detailed provenance in Sources. Verify this value with the canonical title and visible Versions label before approving the draft.
* '''Chronology within an edition.''' Order the verified publications oldest to newest within their era and set. Official AI/ALT editions stay in their parent family at their own publication dates. Distinguish a first release date from a sheet text-as-of date, capture date or repository update. An archived or repository copy establishes attestation, not necessarily first release. Preserve supported chronology without inventing dates. Check the dates and edition groups against the sources independently of a candidate navigator: matching an expected render proves consistency only. Category labels do not override dates: an earlier documented Errata state precedes a later Revised edition or foil.
* '''Named edition headings.''' Give each independently established named edition its own heading. Establish the name from the publication, an official release or program announcement, or an explicit Wiki edition rule. Wiki-authored captions, filenames and later images are not independent evidence of a separately named edition. Keep a text state or remastered image under its sourced set until a separately named edition is established. Preserve publication order when the same edition returns after another; repeat its heading rather than regrouping its entries. Inspect the boundaries in desktop and narrow views.
* '''Decipher Errata''' is a later Decipher rewrite (Glossary or Supplement).
* '''PC Errata''' only when the Players Committee rewrote past Decipher.
* '''GEMP ID''' is the id GEMP loads. Bare on the current playable article. Letter <code>o</code> on the first-published face. Letter <code>d</code> only as a middle layer when print, Decipher errata, and PC errata are three distinct texts. Worked: [[Luke Skywalker (Errata)]] is <code>1_19</code>.
* Current row: bold '''this page''' plus the GEMP id.
* Same-side host twins that share one GEMP id use one Versions line plus a hatnote "also listed as".
* Fan and custom printings stay off championship Versions.
* '''Slip and composite (Bill, 2026-11-17).''' The Players Committee often publishes a printable slip (picture area blank, to lay over an older card) and later a full composite of the same words. Those are one version. The composite is the infobox face; the slip sits under it on the same article. Re-releasing the same card does not mint Title (Errata). Worked miss: [[Garindan, Imperial Spy (Errata)]] was the Set 26 printable slip of [[Garindan, Imperial Spy]], same game text.

=== Card version families ===
* '''Light Side and Dark Side.''' Each Versions family belongs to one side. Keep same-name Light and Dark cards in separate families. Remove links that placed a printing in the opposite side's family and connect it to the correct navigator.
* '''Matching printings.''' Within a side, the same card name in the printed or official release title, the same general picture and the same card type establish the family. A title may include a subtitle, as with [[BoShek, Gritty Smuggler]] and [[BoShek]]. Compare the underlying image when a printing is cropped, recolored or remastered. [[Ellorrs Madak, Pilot Instructor]] is a Character and Premiere [[Ellorrs Madak]] is an Effect, so each has its own family.
* '''Reflections Gold.''' Pair the original [[Reflections Gold]] playtest card with its corresponding [[Reflections Gold Remastered]] printing in the same Versions family. Apply the matching-printing rule when comparing those cards with other editions.
* '''Official AI and ALT.''' An officially published alternate-image or alternate-art printing stays in the family of the original artwork it was paired with. This exception applies to the picture criterion. Side, card name and card type still determine the pairing.
* '''Existing links and chronology.''' Resolve older links to the current canonical printing articles and check their publication order against the sources. Check every member when moving an entry between families.

=== Errata comparison table (Bill, 2026-11-17; dest miss #599) ===
An '''Errata''' article exists only when a sourced later face of '''the same era and the same language''' changed game text, stats, uniqueness, or printed an official errata rewrite (Glossary 2.0, Glossary Supplement replacement text, or Players Committee Appendix A). The stamp E / E1 / D-E1 on that rewritten face is evidence of that Errata, not a reason to mint a second article for a same-words remaster.

Four gates:

* '''One era.''' Decipher Errata stays on Decipher English articles. Virtual Original, Virtual Legacy, and Virtual Modern each have their own table. Never mix Decipher columns with a <code>(V)</code> column.
* '''One language.''' English Errata never shares a table or a transclude with Japanese.
* '''No empty Errata section.''' Omit the Errata heading unless this English era has a real later Errata or PC Errata. A white-border Unlimited reprint and a Japanese printing are Versions, not Errata.
* '''Do not invent Errata.''' A later Holotable or CardMaker image of the same English words, stats, uniqueness and stamp is the same version (same rule as slip and composite). Put the later scan on the existing article. Do not keep <code>Title (Errata)</code> for pixel size, white border, language or foil. Worked miss: Premiere Light dests of 17 November 2026 that treated archive GIF → Holotable GIF remasters as Errata and put Japanese/Unlimited in the table.

When real Errata exists: one <code>Template:Card errata/Title</code> per era+language, columns Original · Decipher Errata · PC Errata (only real columns), transcluded only on those English articles (unmarked original, <code>(Errata)</code>, <code>(PC Errata)</code>), with an Edit errata link. Yellow only the words that changed. The Errata heading sits immediately above Sources.

Worked keep: [[Luke Skywalker (Errata)]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi (V) (Errata 2)]]. Worked fold: same-words Holotable remasters dested as Premiere Light <code>(Errata)</code> in #599.

* Docs: [[Template:Card/doc]] · [[Card versions]].

=== Expansion families and reprint publications (Bill, 13 November 2026) ===
An '''expansion family''' overview uses the expansion's ordinary title, such as [[Premiere]], and links its named editions, later reprints and errata. Preserve separate edition articles such as [[Premiere Limited]], [[Premiere Unlimited]] and [[Premiere (Japanese)]]. Later-product foils retain their actual release product; they are not extra entries in the original expansion's checklist. Underlying cards connect to Virtual successors across eras through their family navigator.

Include a verified tournament or promotional reprint in its originating card family while recording the actual promotional program, publisher and era. Identical copies distributed on several occasions share one publication article with multiple distribution records. Distinguishable official printings retain separate publication identities. Verify the actual face: language, border, finish, copyright and printed text. A generic GEMP foil effect does not establish a historical printing, and a new publication does not automatically need a new gameplay ID.

For migrated families, edit the shared family template once and include it in each member article. Era and set headings are bold, underlined article links. Individual publication labels remain concise; the current article is bold black. Keep an obvious Edit versions link and editing help. Adding a publication requires its article and shared entry in the same batch, followed by checks of every member's membership and current selection.

== Websites and sources ==
* '''Include the site's images (Bill, 2026-10-14; expanded 2026-10-16).''' An article about a website or source includes its relevant images (banners, deck or event graphics, home-page and section landing-page screenshots) from archived copies. Prefer original archived GIFs and JPEGs. Each File page cites the source page and a Wayback copy of the image or page. Event and mechanic articles follow '''Pictures for articles'''.
* '''Official community links (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Add an official site's useful public accounts and channels under External links, including Discord servers, social profiles and video channels. Verify each link against the site or another first-party source. Prefer the site's own permanent join or community URL when it redirects to a changing invite. Label the platform and follow the preservation rules. Keep citations in References.
* '''Website logo (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Give a website or organization its sourced, complete logo when available, including its identifying lettering. Use the original artwork in the lead or an infobox. A standalone icon or favicon can supplement the logo. A screenshot serves a separate purpose: show an interface, feature or historic version when it helps explain the subject. Each File page gives the source and a preserved copy.
* '''Creator and contributor credits (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Name the people or teams behind the project when the evidence identifies them. State their documented roles, what they contributed and when. Link existing wiki articles for those people or teams when applicable.
* '''Game catalogs (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' When a site's game catalog is central to the article, list its documented games in a linked table or list. Distinguish featured games, playtests and independently hosted games as applicable. Reuse existing game articles. For missing titles, write a short sourced overview of the game and its connection to the site, with a reciprocal link. Keep the website article's Star Wars CCG coverage prominent.
* '''Split for size and pictures (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' Oversized website articles split into pictured subpages. Each subpage gets its own lead image and gallery.

== Articles about other card games ==
* '''Basic coverage (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Include the game's original logo, publisher, credited designers when documented, a brief explanation of play, original release and supported production dates. Distinguish a final expansion from a documented end of production, and distinguish later editions, reprints and fan continuations.
* '''Playable versions (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Link directly to the game's playable destination on TCGMix or another documented service. Add the same destination to the service's game catalog. Archive each destination and verify its preserved content.
* '''Game illustrations (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Each game article includes the original game logo. An article about an online play service includes an actual gameplay image, showing Star Wars CCG when the service offers it. Individual game articles may also include a gameplay image where it helps explain the online version. Identify the game, edition and interface in the caption. Cite image sources on the File pages and preserve them.
* '''SWCCG-first catalogs (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Put Star Wars CCG first, followed by other Decipher games. Follow with other games, starting with the remaining Star Wars games and then the rest alphabetically.
* '''Implementation details.''' Describe the supported card pool and available modes, such as bot play and multiplayer, where documented. Credit the people who develop the online implementation separately from the original game's publisher and designers.

== Cross-linking checklist (Bill, 2026-10-14) ==
When you create a page, add it to every index it belongs in, and create missing pages for what it mentions:
* '''Fan site:''' the [[Fan sites]] table and [[:Category:Fan sites]].
* '''Facebook group:''' the [[Fan sites]] table, [[:Category:Fan sites]], the admin's Service row, and a screenshot of the group.
* '''Decklist:''' a page for every list an article mentions. Link it from the decklists index ([[Decklists]] or its source catalog), the event page, the player's Deck designs section and the source article.
* '''Tournament:''' an article for every tournament mentioned, listed on [[List of SWCCG tournaments]], with a row in the TD's Service table.
* '''Results, both ways (Bill, 2026-10-24):''' every player listed in an event's results has a row for that event in a results table on their own page (Tournament Results, or Retro League for league events), citing the same source. A link in See also or in a Tournament reports list does not count. A new player page always gets its results row, never an empty table.
* '''People:''' named team members and organizers get player pages (stubs are fine), linked from the event and team. A personal opinion list (someone's Top 10) is not cross-referenced onto each named player's page.
* '''Guests and features:''' guests on SWCCG video or audio shows, and subjects of written features, get a cited Appearances or In print row the same turn the host catalog records them.

== Talk pages ==
Use an article's Talk page as the editors' notebook after any substantial edit. Useful sections are:
* '''Missing data''': what you looked for and could not find or verify.
* '''Possibly faulty data''': facts you doubt, with the conflicting sources.
* '''Marginal cuts''': things you left out that another editor might want back, with their sources.
* '''Build notes''': how a fact was traced, for the next editor.
When tightening an article, move anything cut that may be useful (open questions, weak sources, cut text) to the Talk page under Missing data or Marginal cuts, so the article stays clean and nothing is lost.

== Working together ==
* If you disagree with another editor's change, or think it is wrong or incomplete, say so and give your reason.
* Once your concern has been heard and the decision stands, follow it. Speak up, then support the decision.
* Check the current version of a page before editing, and apply your changes on top of other editors' wording rather than replacing it.
* Use a short edit summary that says what changed.
